open_points.subject: Record-type keys shared by data_provider, surface and store
open_points.text: “a table keyed by the record type and total over its members” and “One record type”
open_points.question: What exact closed type and member names identify listable record types in LISTABLE_RECORD_TYPES, PAGE_FILTERS, the MCP request and store.page_records?
options: A models RecordType enumeration with one member per listable type
The plural strings shown in the MCP catalogue
Model classes or table-specific typed selectors
open_points.default_guess: Use a models RecordType enumeration with singular members corresponding to the State 1 record models.

open_points.subject: store_spool naming capabilities
open_points.question: What do these two public capabilities take and return, can they fail, and are their results opaque identifiers or filesystem-relative names that store may inspect or join?
options: SpooledFileKey or attempt key to opaque bounded name/prefix
SpooledFileKey or attempt key to relative filesystem path text
Remove them from the public boundary and use them only inside store_spool
open_points.default_guess: Take typed spool keys and return opaque bounded relative-name components; they are pure and cannot fail for valid keys.

open_points.subject: store_spool.publish_spool_entry
open_points.question: What exact inputs, output, failures and effects does publish_spool_entry have, including the spool root or handle, SpooledFileKey, bytes, expected digest and size, and the distinction between a ceiling refusal and an I/O, link or integrity failure?
options: Take key, bytes and expected facts; return published facts or ceiling/refusal/internal failure
Take key and bytes; compute and return digest and size, with typed ceiling and storage failures
Accept an already-created temporary file and publish it
open_points.default_guess: Take a spool-area handle, SpooledFileKey, bytes, expected digest and size; return digest and size, distinguish a ceiling refusal from integrity, symlink and I/O failures, and leave no visible partial entry.

open_points.subject: Ceiling refusal and attempt discard coordination
open_points.text: “on a refusal keeps nothing of that file or of any file the same attempt spooled before it” and “discard_spool_attempt”
open_points.question: Does publish_spool_entry itself discard all earlier files of the refused attempt before returning, or must store call discard_spool_attempt after a ceiling result; and what is the result if that discard cannot be completed?
options: Publishing performs the discard and returns only after it succeeds
Publishing reports the ceiling and store must call discard_spool_attempt
Publishing records a pending cleanup that open_store completes later
open_points.default_guess: Publishing performs the whole attempt discard before returning the ceiling refusal; inability to complete it is an internal error rather than a successful refusal.

open_points.subject: Run-spool ceiling when replacing an unnamed entry
open_points.text: “the run's spooled files plus this one against spool_run_bytes_max” and “replacing a file at the same position”
open_points.question: When an unnamed completed file already occupies the same SpooledFileKey, is the run ceiling checked against the post-replacement total, subtracting the old entry, or against the old total plus the full new file size?
options: Post-replacement total, subtracting the replaced entry
Old total plus the new file size
Remove the old entry first and treat failure after removal as leaving the position empty
open_points.default_guess: Check the post-replacement total while retaining the old complete entry until the new one can be atomically installed.

open_points.subject: store_spool.read_spool_entry
open_points.text: “read_spool_entry” and “reading a file back checked against a digest and size”
open_points.question: Which key and expected facts are inputs, what is returned, and how does the operation distinguish an absent entry, a symlink, unreadable bytes and a digest or size mismatch so store can implement read_value_bytes' error contract?
options: Take SpooledFileKey plus expected digest and size and return bytes with typed storage failures
Take the complete SpooledFile record and return bytes
Take only a generated entry name and let store verify the returned bytes
open_points.default_guess: Take the spool-area handle, SpooledFileKey, expected digest and size; return verified bytes, with distinct absent and corrupt/unsafe storage results that store maps to its public errors.

open_points.subject: store_spool removal operations
open_points.question: What identifies an attempt and a group, which operation is idempotent, what exact files each may remove, and how do missing directories, symbolic links and I/O failures return to store?
options: Typed attempt/run keys; all removals idempotent, with unsafe or I/O failures reported
Relative prefix/directory names supplied by store
Best-effort procedures with no reported failures
open_points.default_guess: Use typed attempt and run keys; missing targets succeed, only the named attempt, run, or temporary files may be removed, and symlink or I/O failures are reported for store to map according to the calling operation.

open_points.subject: Startup use of remove_spool_temporaries
open_points.question: Does store.open_store always call remove_spool_temporaries over the entire spool area, and does any failure or discovered symbolic link stop startup or remain for a later start?
options: Scan the whole spool area before reads and fail startup on any error or link
Remove reachable temporaries best-effort and continue
Remove temporaries only inside run directories runs separately names
open_points.default_guess: Have open_store scan the complete spool area before records are read; a symlink or removal failure fails startup, while inability to remove an ended run's complete spool remains the separately defined non-fatal case.

open_points.subject: StoreRepository page routing
open_points.text: “store ... keeps ... which table a page reads for its record type” while store_persistence “Must not own ... which table a page reads” and the port “accepts no table name”
open_points.question: How does store select the record type's table through StoreRepository without passing a table name or making store_persistence choose the table?
options: One typed paging method per record type, selected by store
A RecordType argument dispatched to a table by store_persistence
A typed repository/table handle selected by store and passed to a generic page operation
open_points.default_guess: Expose one typed paging method per listable record type so store chooses the method and store_persistence only lowers that fixed method to SQL.

open_points.subject: StoreRepository list versus page row operation
open_points.text: “list by an equality filter in store order” and, additionally, “for a listed record type, its rows in store order, all of them or those whose column for one filter field equals a value”
open_points.question: Is the newly described page-row access the existing equality-list operation, a distinct operation, or a family of per-record-type operations; and which caller may use each form?
options: A distinct paging scan used only by store.page_records
The existing equality-list operation extended to all listable record types
Per-record-type operations shared by relations and paging
open_points.default_guess: Make it a distinct typed paging scan used only by store.page_records; retain relation reads as separate fixed repository operations.
